To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the axial and transversal profiles of bright and dark solitions crucially depend on their dispersive and nonlinear properties.

(i) the axial and transversal profiles of bright solitons in matter waves and optical bullets with normal or anomalous dispersion crucially depend on nonlinearity and dispersion properties; (ii) the axial density profiles of bright soliton with anomalous dispersion and of dark soliton with normal dispersion are qualitatively similar and both disappear at a critical density.

the axial and transversal profiles of bright and dark soliton with anomalous and normal dispersion crucially depend on their dispersive and nonlinear properties, and that the critical axial density for the existence of these solitonic matter waves is different for normal and anomalous dispersive solitons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interplay between nonlinearity and dispersion in the presence of transverse confinement.
the study of solitons with positive or negative effective mass in inhomogeneous media.
the study of solitonic matter waves and optical bullets in incompressible and compressible media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in a 1D system, the dispersion of the system plays no significant role in the formation of the soliton.
, in general, the axial and the transverse profiles of solitons with both normal and anomalous dispersions are not necessarily Gaussian.
the dimensionality of the problem plays a crucial role in the dynamics and stability of solitonic matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of harmonic confinement, solitons with positive mass (anomalous dispersion) shrink while those with negative mass (normal dispersion) grow.
, for the same type of nonlinearity, solitons with positive mass are less robust than those with negative mass.
the transverse profile of a soliton in a nonlinear wave equation is a function of the sign of its dispersion, the strength of the nonlinear term, and the strength of the harmonic confinement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
solitons are not only affected by their axial dispersion but also by their transverse one.

, in contrast to the one-dimensional case, soliton stability in higher dimensions is not only determined by the dispersion, but also by the interplay of the nonlinearty and the transverse confinement.

the interplay of nonlinearity and dispersion can lead to very different behaviors in matter waves, depending on the atomic mass, and in light bullets, depending on the sign of the nonlinear refractive index.
